lines.japanese: 「えー、それでは鳳鳴さんの誕生記念日を祝しましてェ」
lines.english: “Well then, a toast to Naru Ohtori's birthday—”

lines.japanese: 「乾杯っ！」
lines.english: “Cheers!”

lines.japanese: 「かんぱーい！」
lines.english: “Cheers!”

lines.japanese: ぶくぶく鳴いている鍋の上で、四つのアルミ缶をぶつけ合った。
lines.english: We knocked four aluminum cans together over the burbling pot.

lines.japanese: ふた昔ぐらい前のトレンディドラマに出てきそうな、ダイニング続きのだだっ広いリビングは、四人ぽっちが鍋を囲んだぐらいじゃ一向にその開放感を損なうことはなかった。
lines.english: The cavernous living room opening onto the dining area looked like something out of a trendy drama from twenty years ago. Four people around a hot pot scarcely made a dent in its spaciousness.

lines.japanese: 「いや、しかしすごい家だねここは」
lines.english: “Still, this is some home.”

lines.japanese: 缶ビールをひと口すすったパルさんが、満天の星空でも見渡すみたいに壁から天井を仰いだ。
lines.english: After a sip of canned beer, Paru looked from wall to ceiling as if surveying a sky crowded with stars.

lines.japanese: 「パルさんもあとでお風呂借りなよ。すっごいよ、超だよ、足伸ばしてバタ足できんだよ」
lines.english: “You should use the bath later, Paru. It's incredible. Beyond incredible. You can stretch your legs all the way out and kick!”

lines.japanese: おくれ毛に艶やかな湿り気を残した風呂上がりの亜衣は、紹介されたばかりの年上女にも気後れすることなく得意げに語る。
lines.english: Fresh from the bath, lustrous moisture still clinging to the loose strands of her hair, Ai proudly regaled the older woman she'd only just met, without a trace of reserve.

lines.japanese: まあ、たしかにすごい家だけど。
lines.english: Well, yes. It was an incredible home.

lines.japanese: 耳がつーんとなる高速エレベーターで地上２８階に打ちあげられた俺たちは、毛足の深い絨毯と石張りの柱が迎える廊下を渡って鳳邸に招きいれられた。
lines.english: The high-speed elevator launched us to the twenty-eighth floor hard enough to make our ears ring. We crossed a corridor lined with deep-pile carpeting and stone-faced columns, then entered the Ohtori residence.

lines.japanese: 面積にしろ調度にしろ何もかもがいちいち庶民規格を上回っている見世物のような５ＬＤＫは、週に三回訪れるという家政婦の手によって隅々まで清潔に保たれていた。
lines.english: The showpiece apartment—five rooms plus living, dining, and kitchen—beat normal-folk standards in size, furnishings, everything. A housekeeper who came three times a week kept every corner spotless.

lines.japanese: 「いまの自分とこもそれなりに気に入っちゃいるけどさ、長い人生、一度くらいはこんな家にも住んでみたいやなあ」
lines.english: “I'm fond enough of the place I've got now, but life's long. Wouldn't mind living somewhere like this once.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、美人は三日で飽きますよー」
lines.english: Well, they say you get tired of beauty in three daaays.

lines.japanese: 分かるような分からないような謙遜を口にした鳴は、両手に挟んだウーロン茶の缶をテーブルに付けたまま微笑んでいた。
lines.english: After making a humble comment that kinda made sense and kinda didn't, Naru smiled, both hands around the oolong-tea can resting on the table.

lines.japanese: 「でも嬉しいです。ここにひとが──」
lines.english: “But I'm happy. Having people here—”

lines.japanese: 「──友達が来たの、初めてなんです」
lines.english: “—This is the first time I've ever had friends over.”

lines.japanese: 「マジでっ？　なんで、もったいなーい！　呼びなよ、ていうか呼んでよがんがん！」
lines.english: “Seriously? Why? What a waste! Invite us! I mean, invite us all the time!”

lines.japanese: 亜衣がでっかいレンゲと長い菜箸を握ったままはしゃぐ。
lines.english: Ai bubbled over, still clutching an enormous ladle and a pair of long cooking chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 「亜衣。使わないなら貸して」
lines.english: “Ai. If you're not using those, hand 'em over.”

lines.japanese: 俺は手を伸ばしてそれを奪った。
lines.english: I reached out and took them from her.

lines.japanese: よく見ると風呂上がりの亜衣は化粧を落としていて、いつもより少しだけ野暮ったく、いつもよりだいぶ愛敬があった。
lines.english: Looking closely, I saw that Ai had washed off her makeup in the bath. She looked a little plainer than usual, and much more endearing.

lines.japanese: 「つーか亜衣さ、おまえ、ほんと元気で良かったな」
lines.english: “Seriously, Ai, I'm glad you're as lively as ever.”

lines.japanese: 「……え、なにそれ。私うるさいとか言われてる？」
lines.english: “...What's that supposed to mean? Are you calling me loud?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そういうこっちゃねえよ。いいんだよ。とにかく良かった良かったっつう話だよ」
lines.english: “Nah, that's not it. It's good. I'm just saying I'm glad. That's all.”

lines.japanese: 俺は菜箸を使って微妙な色の汁に浸かった食材を掻きわけ、好みの具を探しながら言った。湯気の向こうで、亜衣がしかめ面をパルさんに近づけた。
lines.english: As I spoke, I poked through the ingredients in the oddly colored broth with the cooking chopsticks, looking for something I wanted. Across the steam, Ai leaned toward Paru with a frown.

lines.japanese: 「なにあれ？　隼人君もう飲んできたの？」
lines.english: “What's with him? Was Hayato drinking before he came?”

lines.japanese: 「浮かれてんだろ、こんだけ上玉の女に囲まれて」
lines.english: He's giddy 'cause he's surrounded by this many hot women.

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ohhh.”

lines.japanese: 「納得すんなよ。つか、肉ねえよ肉」
lines.english: “Don't agree with her. Anyway, there's no meat. Where's the meat?”

lines.japanese: 陶製のレンゲで鍋の底をさらっても、野菜や練り物ばかりで肉の姿がとんと見えてこない。
lines.english: Even scraping the bottom with the ceramic ladle brought up nothing but vegetables and fish cakes. Not a glimpse of meat.

lines.japanese: いや、肉がない以前に……なんだこのラインナップ。白菜。チクワ。揚げ豆腐。厚揚げ。きりたんぽ。輪切りの大根。なんかよくわかんない魚っぽい肉。
lines.english: Before the missing meat, though... what was this lineup? Napa cabbage. Hollow fish cakes. Fried tofu. Thick-cut fried tofu. Grilled rice sticks. Rounds of daikon. Some kind of fishlike flesh I couldn’t identify.

lines.japanese: 小娘ふたりが終夜営業のスーパーマーケットで揃えてきたという食材は、ひとつ鍋で調理するにはあまりに無秩序で統一感に欠けていた。
lines.english: The ingredients the two girls had assembled at an all-night supermarket were far too lawless and incoherent to cook in one pot.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ。あんさコレ、作ってもらっといてナンだけど、いくらなんでもテーマ性なさすぎじゃね？　ちり鍋なのか、すきやきなのか、おでんなのかハッキリしろよコノヤロウ」
lines.english: Hey. Hey, look, I know you made it for us and all, but this thing has no theme at all, does it? Is it fish hot pot, sukiyaki, or fish-cake stew? Pick one, dammit!

lines.japanese: 「まあ、たしかに……」
lines.english: “Well, he does have a point...”

lines.japanese: 調和も統制もない自由奔放な鍋を見下ろして、料理に明るいパルさんは思わず口ごもっていた。
lines.english: Looking down at the freewheeling pot, devoid of harmony or order, even Paru, who knew her cooking, faltered.

lines.japanese: 「はー、ですよねー。一応これでも私、亜衣ちゃんがおしるこ鍋にしようなどと言って粒あん２００グラムの袋を持ってきたときは、髪をむんずと掴んで引きとめたんですけどー」
lines.english: Yeeah, tell me about it. For your information, when Ai suggested a sweet-red-bean-soup hot pot and brought a two-hundred-gram bag of chunky bean paste, I grabbed her by the hair and stopped her.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、粒あんじゃぜんざい鍋になっちゃうもんな」
lines.english: “Right. With chunky paste, that'd be sweet red-bean stew, not soup.”

lines.japanese: 「え。ツッコミそんなでいいんだ」
lines.english: “What? That's the part you're correcting?”

lines.japanese: 「でも私だって、鳴ちゃんがタイカレー鍋にしようとか言ってココナッツミルク２００グラムの缶を持ってきたときは、喉首に地獄突きを叩きこんで引きとめたよ」
lines.english: “But when Naru proposed Thai-curry hot pot and brought home a two-hundred-gram can of coconut milk, I stopped her with a wrestler’s throat jab.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、タイカレーはナンプラーと香草がなきゃ始まらないもんな」
lines.english: “Right. Thai curry doesn't get out of the gate without fish sauce and herbs.”

lines.japanese: 「え。ツッコミそんなでいいんだ。つか、肉ねえよ肉」
lines.english: “What? That's the part you're correcting? And where's the meat?”

lines.japanese: 俺は思うさま鍋を漁りつくした末、失望という結論に至った。仕方ないのでチクワとハンペンと名前も知れないマイナーな具を拾う。
lines.english: I searched the pot from end to end and found only disappointment. With no meat to be had, I fished out a hollow fish cake, a fluffy fish cake, and some obscure thing I couldn’t even name.

lines.japanese: 「っと、待ちな小僧。最初っからそんないっぱい魚持ってくんじゃないよ。まだダシが出きってないだろ」
lines.english: “Hold it, boy. Don't go taking that much fish at the start. It hasn't given up all its flavor to the stock yet.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　っせえな、肉ねえんだから魚ぐらい大目に見ろよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Shut up. There's no meat, so at least cut me some slack on the fish.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人さん、魚が好きなんですかー」
lines.english: “Do you like fish, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「へー、なんか意外ー」
lines.english: “Huh. That's kind of unexpected.”

lines.japanese: 「好きってかアレだろ、ＤＨＡ。頭が良くなるっていう」
lines.english: “It's not that he likes it. It's the DHA. Supposed to make you smarter.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ohhh.”

lines.japanese: 「納得すんなよ。つか肉がねえんだよ肉が、あァ？」
lines.english: “Don't agree with her. I'm saying there's no meat. No meat, you hear?”

lines.japanese: 俺は菜箸で鍋の縁をぺしぺし叩いて卓上の窮状を愁訴した。買出し係からは異口同音の答弁が返ってきた。
lines.english: I slapped the rim of the pot with the cooking chopsticks, lodging my grievance over the crisis at our table. The purchasing committee returned a unanimous answer.

lines.japanese: 「肉は太る」
lines.english: “Meat makes you fat.”

lines.japanese: 乙女のチームワークだった。
lines.english: The girls were a united front.

lines.japanese: 「いや、入れるだけ入れとけよ。そんなん太りたくねえやつだけ食わなきゃいいんじゃん」
lines.english: “Then put it in anyway. Anyone who doesn't wanna get fat can just choose not to eat it.”

lines.japanese: 「あれば食べる」
lines.english: “If it's there, we'll eat it.”

lines.japanese: なんてはた迷惑なダイエットだ。
lines.english: What a pain-in-the-ass diet.

lines.japanese: 「……ま、いいや。いただきます。超いただきます」
lines.english: “...Whatever. Time to dig in. I am so digging in.”

lines.japanese: 俺は挑戦的に告げると、浅い椀によそった砂漠色の汁に口を付けた。さらりとした塩味の薄汁に、野菜や魚介の雑多な風味が溶けあっていた。
lines.english: I said it like a challenge, then put the shallow bowl of desert-colored broth to my lips. Vegetable and seafood flavors mingled in the thin, lightly salted soup.

lines.japanese: これは……なんだろう。
lines.english: This was... what, exactly?

lines.japanese: 一言で言えば「美味い」なんだろうけど、どうにも一言では済ましたくない品のなさと言うかジャンクっぽさがある。
lines.english: In one word, it was good. But there was a kind of vulgar, junk-food charm to it that “good” didn’t begin to cover.

lines.japanese: 「んん、この味は……玄妙と言うか独創的と言うか……」
lines.english: “Hmm. This flavor is... mysterious, perhaps. Or inventive...”

lines.japanese: パルさんも同じ所感を持ったようだ。喉まで出かかっている「美味い」という賛辞が素直に出てこない、不思議な料理だった。
lines.english: Paru seemed to feel the same way. It was a strange dish: “delicious” was on the tip of her tongue, yet she couldn’t quite bring herself to say it.

lines.japanese: 「どうですか」
lines.english: “How is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶっちゃけて」
lines.english: “Give it to us straight.”

lines.japanese: 小娘ふたりが箸を止めて俺たちをじっと見守っている。
lines.english: The two girls stopped their chopsticks and watched us intently.

lines.japanese: 「……パルさん」
lines.english: “...Paru.”

lines.japanese: 俺は専門家に寸評させようとその名を呼んだが、やつはお椀に顔を近づけ、目線を伏せるように味見を続けていた。
lines.english: I called on the expert for a verdict, but she lowered her face to her bowl and continued tasting with her eyes averted.

lines.japanese: 四つの目が俺ひとりに集中する。
lines.english: Four eyes converged on me alone.

lines.japanese: 「え……いや、まあ……美味えよ？　あぁ、アリっちゃアリじゃね？」
lines.english: “Uh... Well... It's good, you know? Yeah. I mean, it basically works.”

lines.japanese: 思ったことをそのまま口にしたら、やつらは顔を近づけ声をひそめあった。
lines.english: When I said exactly what I thought, they brought their faces together and lowered their voices.

lines.japanese: 「答えに窮している……？」
lines.english: “At a loss for an answer...?”

lines.japanese: 「気を遣われている……？」
lines.english: “Sparing our feelings...?”

lines.japanese: 「なぜかあやふや……」
lines.english: “Vague for some reason...”

lines.japanese: 「どこかうやむや……」
lines.english: “Evasive somehow...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いやいやいや、違げえって違げえって」
lines.english: “No, no, no. That's not it.”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつらの間に手刀を振りおろして、文字通り割って入った。
lines.english: I chopped my hand down between them and, literally, split them apart.

lines.japanese: 「いや、マジで美味えってば。美味えんだけどさ、なんかいろんな味ごちゃ混ぜで落ちつかないっつーかさ、結局のとこコレ何鍋なの？」
lines.english: “No, seriously, it's good. It is. There's just so much jumbled together that the flavor never settles down. What kind of hot pot is this supposed to be?”

lines.japanese: 「土鍋です」
lines.english: “An earthenware one.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、器じゃなくて調理名」
lines.english: “I meant the dish, not the vessel.”

lines.japanese: 「悩むなよ」
lines.english: “Why do you have to think about it?”

lines.japanese: 「亜衣ちゃん、これ何鍋？」
lines.english: “Ai, what kind of hot pot is this?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、オールミックス？」
lines.english: “Um... all-mix?”

lines.japanese: 「しかしアレだね、こんだけ節操なくぶちこんで味の調和が取れてるってのはある意味奇跡だね」
lines.english: Still, chucking all this in with zero restraint and somehow getting the flavors to work... that's kinda a miracle.

lines.japanese: 「やー、そんな奇跡の調理人だなんて」
lines.english: “Oh, you shouldn't call me a miracle-working chef...”

lines.japanese: 「だってさー、買い物カゴ持ってうろうろしてると何でも美味しそうに見えて、ついアレもコレもって入れたくなっちゃうんだよねー」
lines.english: “It's just, when you're wandering around with a shopping basket, everything looks good, and you want to put in this and that and everything else.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それは分かるけどな。でもほら、最初にこうしようっていう目標ぐらいあっただろ？」
lines.english: Yeah, I get that. But c'mon, you at least had some idea what you were aiming for, right?

lines.japanese: 「あー、あー。言われてみればあったような気はしますねー」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Now that you mention it, I feel like we might've had one.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ、あったっけ？」
lines.english: “Really? Did we?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ちょっと待ってください……いま、おぼろげにこう雪国、囲炉裏、黒い鉄鍋……といったイメージソースが脳裏に甦ってますよー」
lines.english: Umm, hang on... I can vaguely feel the image sources coming back to me now: snow country, a sunken hearth, a black iron pot...

lines.japanese: 「雪国？　ああ、石狩鍋か？」
lines.english: “Snow country? Oh, Ishikari hot pot?”

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、石狩鍋ってなんだっけ」
lines.english: “Hayato, what was Ishikari hot pot again?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　いや、知らねえけど、そりゃおまえアレだろ、石狩鍋っつうぐらいだから石狩が入ってる鍋だろ」
lines.english: “Huh? I don't know, but if they call it Ishikari hot pot, it's gotta be a pot with Ishikari in it.”

lines.japanese: 「……え、石狩ってなに」
lines.english: “...Wait. What's an Ishikari?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、石狩鍋はですねー、たしかぶつ切りの鮭と野菜を味噌仕立ての汁で煮込むんですよー。なんかー、元はアイヌのひと達が塩味で調理していたものらしいんですけどー、それに和人が味噌で味付けしましてー」
lines.english: “Ah, Ishikari hot pot is, if I remember right, chunks of salmon and vegetables simmered in miso broth. I heard the Ainu used to cook it with salt, and then the Japanese seasoned it with miso—”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうじゃなくて、どんな形してんの石狩」
lines.english: “No, I mean what shape is an Ishikari?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、石狩ですかー。どうなんでしょうねー。私もまだ見たことないんでー」
lines.english: “Oh, an Ishikari? I wonder. I've never seen one myself.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、私見たことあるかも石狩」
lines.english: “Wait, I think I might've seen an Ishikari!”

lines.japanese: 「まじで！」
lines.english: “Seriously?!”

lines.japanese: それから俺たちは「ぼくの考えた石狩」をテーマに食事を進めた。
lines.english: From there, we carried on with dinner under the theme ‘My Imaginary Ishikari.’

lines.japanese: 食ったら眠くなった。
lines.english: Eating made me sleepy.

lines.japanese: 照明が柔らかで暖房が程よく効いたこの部屋は、ひどく暖かで眠気を誘う。
lines.english: The soft lights and just-right heat made the room really warm and sleepy.

lines.japanese: 俺は床にあぐらをかいて卓を囲んだまま、ソファーのへりに頭をもたせていた。まぶたが重い。
lines.english: I sat cross-legged on the floor around the table, my head propped against the edge of the sofa. My eyelids were heavy.

lines.japanese: 「亜衣ィ、最初の中間でその点数はヤバいだろ」
lines.english: “Ai, getting that score on your very first midterms is bad.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそ、だからそんな感じでどんどん授業ついてけなくなってー、もう春が終わるころにはガッコどーでもよくなっちゃった」
lines.english: “Right? So I fell further and further behind in class, and by the time spring ended, I didn't care about school anymore.”

lines.japanese: すでに鍋は片付けられて、いったん綺麗になったテーブルの上にはちょっと前にデザートと紅茶が並べられた。
lines.english: The hot pot had already been cleared away. A little while ago, dessert and tea had appeared on the table, clean once more.

lines.japanese: コンビニで買ってきたという二個一組の三角ケーキは、ぱさぱさスポンジと缶詰フルーツが見た目を裏切らないチープさだったけど、しっとり練られたクリームは意外に頑張っていた。
lines.english: The convenience-store cake came as two triangular slices in a pack. The dry sponge and canned fruit were exactly as cheap as they looked, though the silky cream was surprisingly good.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれを三、四口で平らげ、林檎の匂いがする紅茶で流しこんだ。女たちは電話番号の交換をしたり、服や食い物や学校の話なんかをしながらちびちび、ちびちび味わっていた。
lines.english: I demolished mine in three or four bites and washed it down with apple-scented tea. The women exchanged phone numbers and talked about clothes, food, and school while savoring theirs in tiny, tiny bites.

lines.japanese: 「でね、ある日ね、ケータイで適当にネットしてたんだー。そしたらいつの間にか、柳木原のギャルサーのサイトに飛んでてー」
lines.english: “So one day, I was just messing around online on my phone. Next thing I knew, I'd landed on the website for a Yanagihara girls' social club.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なにそれー」
lines.english: “What’s that?”

lines.japanese: 「ギャルサークルだろ。あの、よく、グローヴ街とかたむろしてる子ら」
lines.english: “A girls' social club. You know, those girls you always see hanging around Grove Street and places like that.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そんな感じの」
lines.english: “Yeah, that kind of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、同性愛の漫画描いて売ってるひとたち」
lines.english: “Oh, people who draw and sell comics about same-sex romance.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それは違う」
lines.english: “No. That's something else.”

lines.japanese: 「ギャルサーねえ。へえ、そういうのまだ流行ってんだ？」
lines.english: “A girls' club, huh. So those are still popular?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、知らなーい。私、二ヵ月ぐらいで辞めちゃったし。辞めたってゆーか勝手にフェイドアウトだけど」
lines.english: “How should I know? I left after about two months. Well, didn't exactly leave. I just sort of faded out.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、でも一度は入ったんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, but you did join one.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。そのサイトでメンバー募集してたから、なんとなく入会メール送ってみてー」
lines.english: “Yeah. Their site said they were recruiting members, so I sent an application email on a whim.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたらすごいの、幹部の子たち来て──幹部っても、もちろん私と同い年とかせいぜい２コ上とかなんだけど、バーガー屋で面接みたいのあって。無駄に本格的じゃんってゆー」
lines.english: “Then the club leaders showed up—and by leaders I mean girls my age or maybe two years older—and gave me this job-interview thing at a burger place. Like, why is this so needlessly serious?”

lines.japanese: 「へー。そのサークル、どんな系だったの。和サー？」
lines.english: “Huh. What kind of club was it? One of the laid-back ones?”

lines.japanese: 「や、全然。会員三十人ぐらいいて、も、がんがんイベント打ってく系」
lines.english: “Not even close. There were around thirty members, and they were constantly throwing events.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、イベント知ってるー、公民館で手作り漫画の即売会とか仮装パーティー開くんだよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, I know those events. They hold homemade-comic fairs and costume parties at community centers, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、違う。クラブイベントとか」
lines.english: “No, that's different. Club events and stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「ダンパみたいの？」
lines.english: “Like dance parties?”

lines.japanese: 「だねー。それが月イチで、普段の集会は週に二回とかあって。ま、集会っても、基本だべってるだけなんだけど」
lines.english: Yeeah. Those were once a month, and the regular get-togethers were, like, twice a week. Though even calling them get-togethers... we mostly just sat around talking.

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもイベント近くなると、パンフ作ったりパラパラ練習したりして……うん、最初はそーゆーのも楽しかったんだけどね。でも慣れてきて、周りの子のキャラとか掴めてくるとだんだんこう、んー？　みたいな」
lines.english: “Oh, but when an event was coming up, we’d make pamphlets and practice Para Para dances... Yeah, that was fun at first. But once I got used to it and started figuring out what everybody was like, I started going... hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「ノリが合わないって？」
lines.english: “The vibe didn't suit you?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、ノリってゆーかソリってゆーか……」
lines.english: “Not the vibe so much as... we didn’t jibe.”

lines.japanese: 「たとえば私もバカ騒ぎは好きなんだけどー、でも、バリ混みな店で待ってる客いっぱいいんのにガン無視で延々だべりんぐとか、そーゆーのはちょっとキツいんだー。あと、オトコの話ばっかってのもつまんなくて」
lines.english: Like, I love making noise toooo, but sitting forever in a totally packed restaurant, gab-gab-gabbing while flat-out ignoring everyone waiting for a table? That's kinda rough. And I got bored talking about guys all the time.

lines.japanese: 「で、決定打になったのがアレ。会員じゃないんだけどＯＧとか言って出入りしてるフケたねーさんがいて、そいつがバイト紹介するとかゆーんで付いてったら、なんか待ち合わせ場所にハゲたおっちゃんいて」
lines.english: And the last straw was this. This washed-up lady who wasn't even a member kept hanging around calling herself an alum, and she said she'd hook me up with a job, so I went with her—and some bald old dude was at the meeting place.

lines.japanese: 「カラオケボックスでおっちゃんの話ニコニコ聞いてるだけで時給……忘れたけど、お金もらえるとか言われてハァ？でしょ。ちょ、待てっつの。おまえソレ、プチ援交じゃんって」
lines.english: “They tell me I'll get paid by the hour—forget how much—just for sitting in a karaoke box, smiling and listening to the guy talk. Like, what? Hold on. That's basically paid dating.”

lines.japanese: 「えー！　もらったのお金！？」
lines.english: “What! Did you take the money?”

lines.japanese: 「もらうかー！　てか、やるかそんなバイトー！」
lines.english: Like hell I took it! And like hell I'd do a job like thaaat!

lines.japanese: 「わー、亜衣ちゃんえらーい」
lines.english: Waaah, Ai, what a good giiirl.

lines.japanese: 「えらくない！　普通！」
lines.english: “That's not good! That's normal!”

lines.japanese: 「ほー。そんで？　ハゲ親父どうした？」
lines.english: “Huh. So? What happened with Baldy?”

lines.japanese: 「そー、もー聞いてよ！　そしたらなんか私、逆ギレされてー！」
lines.english: Yeah, and listen to thiiis! Then somehow he got mad at meee!

lines.japanese: 「そいつ私の腕がっつり掴んで、金返せガキーとかゆってんの。ありえなくない？　知るかっつーの。そんな金、私もらってねっつーの」
lines.english: “He grabs my arm and starts yelling, ‘Give me my money back, brat!’ Can you believe that? Like I know anything about it. Nobody gave me any money.”

lines.japanese: 「しかもＯＧのフケ女、ひとりで逃げてるし！　もぉ、超でしょ？　超、ありえんてぃーでしょ？　ほんっと、いまだからこんなネタ話だけど、そんとき実際ちょー恐くて。私もう、泣き寸だもん」
lines.english: “And the washed-up alumna runs away by herself! It was beyond, right? Like, completely ridic, right? I can tell it as a funny story now, but at the time I was seriously terrified. I was one second from tears.”

lines.japanese: 「逃げて！　亜衣ちゃん逃げて！」
lines.english: “Run! Ai, run!”

lines.japanese: 「ふん。そんで」
lines.english: “Hmph. And then?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……したら、なんか、このひとが通りがかって救けてくれたの」
lines.english: “Yeah... Then this guy happened to pass by and saved me.”

lines.japanese: 俺はいつの間にか目を閉じて俯いていたみたいだ。ふと女たちの声が途切れたので何事かと頭を上げたら、六つの目がこちらに向けられていた。
lines.english: At some point I had apparently closed my eyes and let my head droop. The women's voices abruptly stopped; when I raised my head to see why, six eyes were fixed on me.

lines.japanese: 「え……あぁ、俺？」
lines.english: Huh...? Oh, me?

lines.japanese: 寝起きみたいなくぐもった声が出てしまった。
lines.english: My voice came out muffled, as if I'd just woken up.

lines.japanese: 「てかさ、一応それより前んときから、翔さん繋がりでお互い顔ぐらいは知ってたけど。でも、ちゃんと名前とか聞いて友達っぽくなったのは、あのときからだったんだよね」
lines.english: I mean, we knew each other's faces before then through Kakeru and stuff. But that was when we actually traded names and kinda became friends, y'know?

lines.japanese: 「私的に隼人君の印象ってそれまでは、なんかヘンなやつーって、そんだけだったんだけど。それ以来、なんかヘンだけどいいやつーって風になって」
lines.english: “Before that, my impression of Hayato was just, ‘He's kind of weird.’ Afterward, it became, ‘He's weird, but he's a good guy.’”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、ヘンとか言うな。フィクションでもいいから、そこは綺麗にまとめとけよコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Don’t call me weird. Make something up if you have to—give the story a nice ending, dammit.”

lines.japanese: いきなり一同の視線を浴びている状況がなんとなく照れくさくて、俺は一応そのときのことを覚えてはいたけど、ついとぼけて後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: Everyone suddenly looking at me was kinda embarrassing. I remembered what happened, but I played dumb and scratched hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 寝惚け声にひどくマッチする身振り。亜衣が人差し指の第二関節を唇に付けた姿勢で、凝らすように俺を見据えていた。いや、見るな。
lines.english: The gesture went perfectly with my sleep-muddled voice. Ai pressed the middle knuckle of her index finger to her lips and studied me. Don’t look.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、ドラにしちゃいいことしたじゃないか。なあ鳴」
lines.english: “Well, that was decent of you, for Drac. Right, Naru?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、理想のタイプは正義の味方ですよー」
lines.english: Yeees. My ideal type is a heeero.

lines.japanese: 「……っせえな、偶然だよ偶然。偶然通りかかっただけだっつーの。しょーがねえだろ、だって偶然そんな出くわしちゃったらよう」
lines.english: “...Shut up. It was a coincidence. That's all. I just happened to be passing. What else was I supposed to do when I happened to run into something like that?”

lines.japanese: わけもなく露悪的に振るまって、俺はまた目を閉じた。頭を反らせてソファーの座面に倒す。
lines.english: For no good reason, I played the bad guy and closed my eyes again. I tipped my head back onto the sofa cushion.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、眠みぃっつーの、ったく」
lines.english: “God, I'm sleepy. Damn it.”

lines.japanese: わざとらしく口に出してはみたものの、それは事実だった。パルさんのバンの中でちょっとばかり仮眠を取ったぐらいじゃ、睡魔は完全に撃退できなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: I made a show of saying it aloud, but it was true. The short nap in Paru's van hadn't been enough to drive sleep away entirely.

lines.japanese: 「あ、お休みになりますー？　掛けるもの持ってきましょうかー？」
lines.english: “Oh, are you going to sleep? Want me to bring you something to cover up with?”

lines.japanese: 鳴が腰を上げかけたのが音と気配で分かる。
lines.english: I could tell from the sound and movement that Naru had started to get up.

lines.japanese: 「あァ……あーいや、いいです……」
lines.english: “Huh...? Oh, no, I'm fine...”

lines.japanese: まどろみの幕が下りてくるのを感じながらも丁重に断った。
lines.english: Though I could feel the curtain of drowsiness descending, I politely declined.

lines.japanese: もう夜明けは遠くない。深い眠りに落ちるのは危険だ。目を覚ましたとき、タカシに替わってしまっている可能性が否めない。だから、ここでこうしてうたた寝してるぐらいがちょうどいいんだ。
lines.english: Dawn was not far off. Falling into a deep sleep was dangerous. I couldn't rule out waking to find Takashi had taken my place. A little doze right here was just enough.

lines.japanese: 「私のベッド使ってもらってもいいですよー」
lines.english: You can use my bed if you waaant.

lines.japanese: 「いや平気……寝ないから……たぶん……」
lines.english: “No, I'm fine... Not gonna sleep... probably...”

lines.japanese: 「寝ろ寝ろ、男なんか寝ちまえ」
lines.english: Sleep, sleep! Men can just go to sleep already.

lines.japanese: 亜衣の捨て台詞が聞こえた。俺はそのささやかな呪いをしっかり受けとめながら、身を起こしたままの眠りに滑りおちていった。
lines.english: I heard Ai’s parting shot and let her little curse settle over me. Still sitting upright, I slipped into sleep.

lines.japanese: 暖房が程よく効いたこの部屋は、ひどく暖かで眠気を誘う。
lines.english: With its perfectly judged heat, the room was terribly warm, terribly conducive to sleep.
